notes: Inbound SMB - HelpStream Labs building an in-app support assistant. Self-serve signup -> hit parsing issues when switching to JSON mode + streaming and enabling function/tool-calling. Engineer notes: "stream often emits partial JSON (truncated object), sometimes extra trailing commas, and function_call payloads don't match our client schema (missing or renamed fields)". Using Node.js SDK + SSE. Reported ~30-50% of streamed responses fail JSON.parse on client side when reassembling chunks. They tried buffering until "\n\n" but still see partial objects. Also seeing mismatched types for tool arguments (string vs object). Cost sensitivity moderate; plan to stay on hosted API if reliability OK. Quoted: "If we can't get predictable structured outputs we can't ship the product - needs deterministic function_call behavior". AE asked SE to run POC focusing on: 1) streaming chunk framing best practices, 2) recommended server-side & client-side reassembly patterns, 3) enabling strict schema validation or helper middleware, 4) fallback policy suggestions (non-stream fallback or post-hoc JSON repair). Security has standard asks (SSO, SOC2).
requirements_summary: Workload: real-time support chat with tool-calls (ticket creation, KB search) + structured JSON output for downstream automation
Latency target: <200ms token latency for interactive agents; end-to-end response <1s preferred
Throughput: expected initial concurrency 30-50 agents, burst to 100
Cost sensitivity: moderate; SMB budget, prefers hosted API until scale justified
Model preferences: open/curated models acceptable; need consistent function_call behavior across model variants
Routing/fallback: prefer automatic fallback to non-streaming full-response on parse failure; consider lower-cost model variants for non-critical flows
Security: SSO/SAML and audit logs required for later procurement; environment = public cloud
